extra_misconceptions.fact: Solvents thin the resin and break down the skin barrier, accelerating chemical absorption into the bloodstream; use soap and water instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Washing uncured epoxy off bare skin with acetone or alcohol is the safest way to remove sticky residue.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Particulate masks only trap solid fibers; filtering volatile organic vapors from liquid resins requires an NIOSH organic vapor cartridge.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A disposable N95 dust mask protects the lungs from both sanding dust and volatile styrene fumes during layup.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Bulk uncured resin generates intense exothermic heat in a confined bin and can ignite paper or plastic trash if not cured flat first.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Leftover mixed resin can be poured directly into a trash can immediately after finishing a composite layup.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Amine hardeners and solvents rapidly permeate thin latex, whereas nitrile resists chemical penetration and prevents skin sensitization.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Latex exam gloves provide the same chemical barrier as nitrile gloves when handling liquid epoxy hardeners.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Fiberglass is an excellent electrical insulator, whereas carbon fiber conducts electricity and causes short circuits or galvanic corrosion.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: All fiber-reinforced plastics act as electrical insulators and can be safely used around high-voltage lines.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Composites are anisotropic and carry maximum loads along their fiber axes, requiring multi-angle plies to resist off-axis shear forces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Composite laminates have identical tensile strength in every direction just like isotropic steel or aluminum sheets.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Carbon fiber acts as a noble cathode when paired with aluminum in saltwater, rapidly corroding the metal unless isolated by fiberglass.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Composite materials never suffer from chemical degradation or corrosion when fastened to metal hardware in marine water.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Matrix and reinforcement phases remain physically distinct in a finished composite, bonding mechanically and chemically at their interface.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Metals and polymers melt together during composite manufacturing to form a single homogeneous chemical compound.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes a true composite material from a metallic alloy like steel or brass at the microscopic level?
Why is it dangerous to bolt carbon fiber panels directly onto bare aluminum aircraft frames without an insulating barrier?
Which structural component inside natural wood acts as the matrix, and which part serves as the tensile reinforcement?
Under what loading condition does a unidirectional composite laminate fail at a fraction of its rated tensile strength?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Epoxy requires an exact stoichiometric ratio; excess hardener leaves unreacted amine in the matrix, leaving the cured part soft and brittle.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Adding extra amine hardener to a two-part epoxy batch makes the resin cure faster and produces a stronger part.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Carbon fiber is very stiff but brittle under sharp impact, whereas aramid fibers absorb high impact energy without shattering.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carbon fiber has higher impact toughness and elongation before breaking than aramid or E-glass reinforcements.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Polyester resin cures poorly and forms weak secondary bonds over cured epoxy, whereas epoxy adheres reliably over cured polyester surfaces.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Polyester resin bonds to cured epoxy laminates with the same chemical cross-linking strength as fresh epoxy.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thermoset polymers form irreversible cross-linked molecular networks during curing and char or decompose rather than melting when reheated.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Thermoset resins like polyester and epoxy can be melted down and remolded into new shapes for easy recycling.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to a cured thermoset epoxy matrix vs a thermoplastic resin when reheated above its glass transition temperature?
Why does aramid fiber excel at stopping ballistic impacts yet perform poorly under axial compressive structural loads?
What measurement confirms that a two-part epoxy system has been proportioned to its exact stoichiometric mix ratio?
Which SDS section details the required spill containment and hazardous waste disposal rules for uncured vinyl ester resin?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Atmospheric pressure compresses the fiber stack inside the sealed bag, squeezing excess resin and trapped air into the breather fabric.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Vacuum bagging a wet layup works by sucking air bubbles completely out of the solidifying resin through the plastic film.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Prepreg fabrics contain pre-catalyzed resin that slowly cures at room temperature, requiring sub-zero freezer storage to preserve shelf life.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Prepreg carbon fiber cloth can be stored on open shop shelves at room temperature for months before autoclave molding.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Structural repairs require sanding a shallow beveled scarf taper so new overlapping fabric plies transfer shear loads into each original layer.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Structural damage in a composite hull can be restored to full strength by filling the hole with thick chopped-strand putty.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Pultrusion only produces straight constant-cross-section profiles, whereas filament winding wraps fibers over rotating mandrels for tanks.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pultrusion and filament winding are interchangeable manufacturing methods for producing hollow spherical pressure vessels.

extra_socratic_questions: What happens to the fiber-to-resin volume ratio when a manufacturer switches from open hand layup to vacuum-assisted infusion?
Which closed-molding process pulls continuous resin-soaked fiber rovings through a heated steel die to make constant profiles?
Why is a tapered scarf joint used instead of a butt joint when repairing a punctured structural composite skin?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unreinforced resin is brittle and weak in tension; excess resin adds dead weight and cracks easily under flexing without fiber support.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Applying a thicker coat of resin over the fiberglass cloth increases the tensile strength of the finished project.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Rapid whipping folds air bubbles into the viscous mixture, creating porous voids that weaken the cured matrix; stir slowly scraping the sides.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Vigorous whipping when stirring resin and hardener ensures the fastest and most uniform composite cure without defects.

extra_misconceptions.fact: White chalky patches in cured fiberglass reveal dry, resin-starved fibers where trapped air prevented complete wet-out of the weave.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Opaque white streaks inside cured fiberglass laminate indicate areas where the glass fibers are strongest and densest.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Machining cured composites releases sharp respirable glass or carbon dust that irritates skin and lungs, requiring goggles and a respirator.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Sanding and trimming cured composite edges can be done safely without PPE once the liquid resin has fully hardened.

Why does adding excess resin beyond what saturates the reinforcement cloth weaken the final cured composite project?
What acoustic difference during a coin tap test distinguishes a solid laminate from an internal delamination void?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Certified composite technicians, mold makers, and autoclave operators enter the field through community college programs and apprenticeships.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every career in the composites industry requires a four-year university degree in materials science or aerospace engineering.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Composites lack a plastic yield zone and remain elastic until they reach their ultimate load, where they fracture suddenly or delaminate.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carbon fiber sporting goods like bicycle frames and hockey sticks bend permanently just like aluminum when overloaded.

extra_misconceptions.fact: NDT specialists ultrasonically scan newly manufactured aerospace and wind-energy structures before delivery to verify zero internal voids.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Non-destructive testing technicians only inspect composite parts after a catastrophic structural failure occurs in service.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Cured thermoset sporting goods cannot be melted in municipal plastics recycling and require specialized pyrolysis or mechanical grinding.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Fiberglass and carbon fiber recreational equipment can be disposed of in standard municipal recycling bins at end of life.
